items.text: Oil prices flat week-over-week (WTI 89.5, Brent 92.9) despite lingering geopolitical premium, but structural support remains. For leveraged energy credits and high-yield energy M&A, elevated rates (UST 10Y 5.04%) now matter more than commodity volatility in refinancing and valuation.

Claims ticked up to 203k (from 202k); unemployment holds at 4.1%, yet payrolls jumped 165k in October (prev 60k), signaling data quality noise or frontloading. Wage growth slowing (AHE 3.12% from 3.16%) suggests labor cost pressure easing—important for covenant headroom in cyclical credits.

Core PCE stuck at 2.57% YoY (through Sept), headline 3.72%; PPI accelerating at 6.52% (Oct). The curve flattened sharply (10Y/2Y 28bp) as market prices Fed hold through year-end. Sticky goods inflation and energy pass-through risk weigh on spec-grade real yields and DIP availability.

Fed paused at 4.0% with curve control priced flat-to-higher; ECB deposit rate at 2.50% with 94% odds of 25bp hike Dec 17. Cross-curve repricing (US 10Y down 11bp week) reflects growth concerns, not inflation relief. Rising refinance pressure on floating-rate debt and bond call dynamics.

HY OAS widened 18bp to 352bp; IG OAS also up 4bp to 94bp; CCC OAS spiked 51bp to 1361bp—the sharpest move. High-beta credits repricing off election volatility and recession hedging. Event-driven and distressed dislocations intensifying; sponsorship drying up.

GDPnow slipped to 3.21% from 3.27% and Q3 real GDP was 3.4% YoY. Existing home sales cratered to 3.75M annualized (lowest since 2010), down 5.5% MoM and 8.8% YoY as 30Y mortgage rates hit 7.28%. Housing stocks vulnerable; builder credits at risk if rates stay elevated.

UMich sentiment rebounded to 51.5 final (Nov, from 48.0 Oct) post-election, but remains in first percentile historically. Year-ahead inflation expectations crashed 100bp to 3.7%, signaling deflation risk priced in. Consumer is on edge; ISM Services held 54.5 (miss), new orders dropped.

themeCards.title: Housing Market Structural Weakness
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales at 16-year low (3.75M), mortgage rates above 7%, inventory rising, first-time buyer share collapsed to 29% from 32% YoY. Supply/demand mismatch and 'lock-in' effect entrench market dysfunction.
themeCards.relevance: Real estate debt (CMBS, agency RMBS, builder bonds) under pressure; residential construction finance at risk. Spec-situation distressed refi and forbearance opportunities emerging in acquisition finance backed by illiquid collateral.

themeCards.title: CCC Distress & Credit Bifurcation
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS widened 51bp to 1361bp; HY OAS +18bp to 352bp while IG +4bp to 94bp. High-beta, low-covenant credits being repriced aggressively; sponsorship drying up post-election volatility.
themeCards.relevance: Deepest dislocations in CCC single-B, junior cap, and covenant-lite. Special situations investors positioned for 2027 refinance wall, liability management events, and potential take-privates at distressed valuations.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction
themeCards.statusLine: Official NBS PMI fell below 50 (49.3 Oct), signaling contraction; SME PMI at 47.5. Weak new orders and demand offset policy stimulus. Services and high-tech remain resilient.
themeCards.relevance: Spillover risk to US export growth, commodity prices, and supply chains; credit stress in Chinese corporates widens yield spreads for offshore debt. Opportunities in Asian credit dislocations and leveraged China-exposed US corporates.

themeCards.title: Yield Curve Flattening & Refinance Wall
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y/2Y spread at 28bp, narrowest in 18 months; 10Y down 11bp week to 5.04%. Market pricing Fed hold and growth deceleration; floating-rate and short-duration borrowers face refinance shock and roll-down risk.
themeCards.relevance: Leveraged buyout debt, project finance, and sponsor-backed floating-rate notes all face repricing. Early-stage covenant waivers and waiver fees; refinance-driven M&A and restructuring opportunities abundant in 2027.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Goods Inflation
themeCards.statusLine: PPI at 6.52%, up 23bp MoM; core PCE flat at 2.57% YoY but import and goods prices rising. Services inflation slowing, but input cost pass-through risk in transportation, chemicals, autos.
themeCards.relevance: Margin pressure in cyclicals (autos, transpo, chemicals, construction); refinance risk for leveraged industrials at higher rates with shrinking EBITDA cover. Covenant tightness and CDS tightness divergence create arb/dislocation trades.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Rebound vs Structural Weakness
themeCards.statusLine: UMich sentiment jumped to 51.5 final (Nov, highest in 3 months) on post-election optimism, but year-ahead inflation expectations collapsed to 3.7% (100bp down)—signaling deflation hedging, not confidence. Retail ex-autos YoY still elevated at 8.14%.
themeCards.relevance: Divergence suggests consumer is bifurcated: confidence in politics/valuations but hedging macro risk. Retail and consumer discretionary credits face demand volatility; consumer staples/defensive credits may outperform if pessimism re-emerges.

ecb.delta: Unchanged since Sept; 94% odds of +25bp hike on Dec 17

chinaPMI.delta: Oct NBS official PMI below 50-point expansion threshold, down from 50.1 in Sept

ismServices.delta: Oct reading missed forecast of 54.8; new orders fell from 59.8 to 55.9

retailSales.delta: Retail ex-autos YoY data current through Oct (8.14%, up from 7.65% Sept)

existingHome.delta: Oct 2026: lowest since Aug 2010; down 5.5% MoM, 8.8% YoY

regime.label: Transition — late-cycle moderating
regime.detail: Rates held, curve flat-to-inverted priced, credit bifurcating (CCC distressed), housing collapsing, labor cooling, core inflation sticky but expectations falling. Fed on hold into year-end; risk-off repricing in high-beta credit; special situations window widening.
